value.body: Dental surgeon (or dental officer) posts in state health departments — district hospitals, community health centres and some primary health centres. States recruit through their Public Service Commission or a health recruitment board. Teaching posts in government dental colleges are filled separately and usually need an MDS.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: BDS from a DCI-recognised college, a completed internship and State Dental Council registration. Apply when your state's PSC or health recruitment board notifies posts; selection is by written exam, sometimes with an interview, and a few states select on merit. Domicile, local-language and age rules usually apply.

value.title: At a glance
items: Posts are limited and openings come irregularly, so many graduates also prepare for MDS (NEET-MDS) or work in private practice.
Some states hire contract dental surgeons under NHM, with different terms from regular posts.
Central posts, such as the Army Dental Corps and central health services, are recruited separately.
